answer: Cost is charged per lineage, not per account. Each identity carries a provenance pigment stamped at funding, and the ledger treats a cluster as one walnut however many shells it is packed into, so splitting across n wallets buys nothing. The toll is a terrace, each step steeper: the n-th clone pays strictly more than the first, so total cost grows super-linearly in n. Shedding the mark needs separate capital origin, an outside counterparty with its own history, which a farm cannot mint in parallel; laundering through fresh wallets re-inherits it, since ancestry is stained, not the address.
